title: Deep learning identified minimal mutations for cross-reactive anti-PD-L1 antibodies
summary: A deep-learning model trained on deep-mutational-scanning sequence–binding data selected minimal mutation combinations for a human anti-PD-L1 antibody with mouse cross-reactivity. Variants with four to five substitutions showed in-vitro and cellular binding comparable to conventionally recombined variants with 13–15 substitutions; the paper also reports blockade assays and therapeutic activity in a mouse tumor model. These are preclinical antibody-engineering results, not evidence of human efficacy. The preprint reports patent applications related to the subject matter.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model trained on deep-mutational-scanning sequence–binding data
organization: Université Paris-Saclay; CEA; INRAE; CNRS; Inserm; Institut Agro Rennes

evidence.tested: The preprint reports in-vitro and cellular binding properties of selected variants, PD-1/PD-L1 competition/blockade assays, epitope mapping and mouse tumor-model assessment. The 4–5 substitution variants are compared with highly mutated variants requiring 13–15 substitutions.
evidence.unknown: Mouse-model activity is preclinical and does not establish human therapeutic efficacy. The preprint reports patent applications relevant to the work; no freedom-to-operate or patent-priority conclusion is made.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning model trained on DMS-derived sequence-binding data selected minimal mutation combinations for experimental antibody characterization.
